correctness.rationale: Dirichlet beta shifting proves the all-real-power exact mixed tail identity. Strict convexity and positive endpoint deviations give precisely two conditional-mean level roots, hence one covariance threshold. At power two, two independently checked beta integration-by-parts identities yield the exact root; shifted beta concentration yields the high-power limit. The standalone verification passed 860 assertions (690 exact rational, 150 noninteger quadrature/sign, 20 high-order numerical). Finite computations are corroboration, not universal proof.

originality.rationale: Examined the most relevant accessible foundational papers on Simpson and generalized Tsallis index priors, including the finite symmetric Dirichlet case; compared claim implications rather than titles, plus semantic searches of published mathematical records. Those sources give concentration moments, not a mixed abundance-exceedance-count/power-concentration covariance, its all-order unique crossing or its expected-one high-order limit. Prior general machinery allows derivation but does not directly assert or logically entail the proposed sign classification without an additional threshold-weighted calculation. Priority cannot be proven exhaustively.

value.rationale: Threshold-count richness at a chosen relative abundance and generalized Simpson/Tsallis power concentration are independently meaningful ecological/compositional statistics. The result determines the complete sign transition for every power order, gives an explicit Simpson threshold, and identifies the limiting abundance threshold where exactly one species is expected to be abundant. The dependence law is not available from marginal diversity moments alone; it explains how counts of abundant categories shift from opposing to reinforcing total concentration.
